title: The failed coup of 11 March
summary: On 11 March 1975 officers associated with António de Spínola moved against the left of the Armed Forces Movement, with an air attack on the RAL-1 artillery barracks in Lisbon at its centre; the attempt found little support and collapsed the same day. Spínola left the country that evening, first for Spain and then for Brazil. The reaction was immediate and went far beyond the plotters: the Council of the Revolution was created within days, the banks and insurance companies were nationalised, and the officers who had wanted a slower course lost the argument. Whether the day was a coup attempt, a provocation, or a badly judged reaction to a rumour of a right-wing plot is still argued; the shift in the balance of power that followed is not. It is in the atlas because the largest economic changes of 1975 descend from a failed operation rather than from a decision taken on its merits.
